claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure containing dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The starting alloy has high strength.
The starting alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittle behavior.
Dislocation pile-ups at coarse internal boundaries produce local stress concentrations in the untreated alloy.
The local stress concentrations caused by pile-ups lead to microcracking and brittle or catastrophic failure under tensile loading.
Approximately 50% cold rolling followed by annealing at about 800°C for 10 minutes will refine the lamellar colonies.
The thermomechanical treatment will increase the density of high-angle internal boundaries.
High-angle internal boundaries act as effective barriers to dislocation transmission.
Increasing the number of high-angle internal boundaries will distribute dislocation pile-ups across more sites.
Distributing dislocation pile-ups across more sites will reduce local stress concentrations.
Reduced local stress concentrations will limit microcracking and catastrophic failure.
The treatment will significantly increase room-temperature tensile ductility, as reflected by increased strain or elongation to failure.
The treatment will maintain or slightly increase strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The prediction applies to room-temperature tensile deformation.
The treatment may be applicable under cyclic and fatigue loading.

contradictions.description: The conditions field includes cyclic and fatigue loading as applicable conditions, whereas the boundary field restricts the prediction to room-temperature tensile deformation and states that behavior under other loading conditions is uncertain.
